acceptedWorkstreams.title: Answer the standard questionnaire from evidence we already hold, and list the gaps in writing
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Institutional reviewers ask roughly the same forty questions: hosting and region, encryption in transit and at rest, backup frequency and restore testing, retention and deletion, access control, subprocessors, incident notification, and business continuity. Answer each from something that exists rather than a template aspiration, and where nothing exists, write "not yet" with what it would take. Work: the forty questions, the answer, the source, and the gap list. Deliver it as the internal master document the public page is written from, because the page should never say more than this.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Publish the subprocessor list and the data flow before a reviewer has to ask
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The first question a university asks after "where is it hosted" is "who else touches the data". Work: list every third party that receives or stores customer data — hosting, email, payments, analytics, support tooling, AI providers — with its purpose, the data it sees, and where it processes it. Confirm each from configuration or contract rather than memory. Deliver the table, the note on which entries still need a contract or a region confirmed, and the public version of it with the commercial detail removed.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Rehearse one real review: send the pack to a reviewer and record every follow-up question
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A security page is finished when a reviewer stops asking, not when it is published. Work: give the pack to one person who has actually run an institutional review, ask them to answer the questionnaire using only the page, and record every question the page could not answer, every answer they did not believe, and every document they asked for. Then fix the page in the order they raised things. Deliver the transcript of the gaps, the changes made, and the second pass result. This is the only test that predicts whether the next review stalls.

upvotes.reason: "Rehearse one real review: send the pack to a reviewer and record every follow-up question" has a scriptable structure, so it can be produced and reviewed rather than left open-ended. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Use the HECVAT Lite question set as the page's skeleton, so reviewers find their questions in the order they ask them
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Many university IT teams send EDUCAUSE's HECVAT (Lite version) or a close local copy. Approach: map HECVAT Lite's sections (company, data, hosting, encryption, backups, access, incident response, subprocessors) to the page headings; answer each with the checked fact and its source, or "not known yet" with an owner. Add a Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 section and the DPA download. Done: the page draft in HECVAT order, a filled HECVAT Lite sheet the team can attach to replies, and the list of unanswered questions. This turns many questionnaires into one prepared answer.

upvotes.reason: Anchoring 'Answer a university security questionnaire without a call, by Fri 27 Nov' in verified operational workflows accelerates cohort onboarding.
Using the reviewers' own question order means they find each answer where they expect it instead of hunting through a page organised for us.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Write the data processing agreement from the actual data flows, not from a downloaded template
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A DPA that contradicts the product is worse than none, because a reviewer will notice during implementation. Work: take the data-flow list, then write the clauses that matter for this product: controller and processor roles, what happens to a cohort's files after it closes, deletion timelines, subprocessor changes, breach notice, and where data is stored. Mark every clause that needs a lawyer or a named owner before it can be signed. Deliver the draft, the clause-by-clause note on what it rests on, and the list of decisions only the company can make.

upvotes.reason: "Write the data processing agreement from the actual data flows, not from a downloaded template" has a defined audience and a clear done-state, and it addresses something the site does not currently say. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.
A DPA built from the real data flows avoids contradictions a reviewer will find during implementation; template text is the usual source of those contradictions.
